text.p: Following are the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Tuesday.
- Government to double social welfare spending next year in a bid to improve living standard of workers and pensioners.
- President Tudjman names general Pavao Miljavac the new army Chief of Staff.
- Russian ministry for oil and Transneft company negotiate with Croatia's INA to buy shares of the Adriatic pipeline so as to transport 14 million tonnes of Russian crude per year.
- Croatia's privatisation described as moderately sucessful in a study by EBRD which asessed quality of privatisation process in the countries of transition.
- Croatian and Slovenian bankers with 150 billion lira savings in the recently failed Banco di Credito di Trieste to find out about the destiny of their money this week.
- Compulsory retirement age to be 65 according to amendments to the pension law.
- New Istrian thermo-electric power plant to be completed by Germany's RWE Energie and HEP, esimated to generate 75 million DM income a year with an average profit rate of 20 percent.
- The government proposes to subsidise housing and utilities costs to the poorest citizens under a new three-year welfare programme.
- Interview with Miomir Zuzul, ambassador to Washington: Clinton will not change the U.S. policy towards Zagreb.
- A firm from Labin in Istria patented a new method of combatting enviromentally dangerous algae Caulerpa taxifolia by vacuuming it from the sea bed. -- Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
